categories.summary: No new attacks on US bases, warships or tankers were found in the last day (checked today's attack headlines and a search for new attacks). This week Iran hit a US radar site in Bahrain, fired drones at a US base in Kuwait (shot down), and a tanker was attacked in Hormuz. A headline about Russian missiles crashing in Poland appears to refer to an earlier incident (July); no new one was found. Taiwan and Korea show no new warning signs.

categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal. Forecast markets put a Russian or US nuclear test this year at under 3%.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: Cybernews: Visa confirms cyberattack as hackers claim JPMorgan hit too
Quartz: Hackers leak Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan data via vendors

categories.summary: The run of big overseas outages and hacks continues (Microsoft, Chase, Apple, a US spy-agency network, and the Visa/Mastercard/JPMorgan supplier hack), but nothing new hit Australia today. One report says the leaked card-hack files list some Australians but no card numbers; the hack was by a criminal gang, not a state. The collector links it to a 'China campaign' touching Australia, but that link is wrong: the China-linked activity is spying through a now-patched VMware server flaw and a new FBI warning about an AI hacking tool. Suspected Iran-linked attacks on fridges and small water systems stay in Europe and the US. Australian phones, banks and the grid are normal.

sources.title: WHO: Ebola (Bundibugyo) - DRC, Kenya and Nigeria

categories.summary: WHO reports Ebola in parts of Africa, MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and a pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia; none is spreading toward Australia. A stomach bug on a US cruise ship is routine. Two Adelaide emergency departments (Flinders, Noarlunga) are very busy, below the level that would suggest an outbreak.

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is Moderate today and tomorrow, with no fire bans or CFS warnings near home. Some outback roads remain closed by flooding.

categories.summary: Hormuz is still effectively shut (100+ ships a day before the war; about 2 a day now). Brent oil fell another 3% to about US$89, though a weaker Australian dollar blunts the saving; SA pump prices are down a few cents. Supply is tight but there are no shortages in SA.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: The US 'fear gauge' (VIX) rose another 14% to 32, gold fell over 4% and the Australian dollar slipped to 66.3 US cents; Wall Street is on its longest losing run since 2024. Jittery, but no sign of a crash or bank trouble.

headline: A second quiet night in the Gulf: no new attacks on US bases or tankers were found, but the Strait of Hormuz stays shut, so fuel stays dear.
summary: No new attacks on US bases, warships or tankers were found in the last day; the latest were Iran's strikes on Bahrain and Kuwait and a tanker attack in Hormuz earlier this week. Oil eased again to about US$89, but share markets are jumpy (the US 'fear gauge' rose another 14%) and the Australian dollar slipped to 66 US cents. One report says leaked files from the Visa and Mastercard supplier hack list some Australians, but no card numbers; the hack was by a criminal gang and mostly hit US customers. Near home it is quiet: fire danger in the Hills is Moderate today and tomorrow, with a cool, gusty change on Monday.
